title: Zonal diversion chronicle - scratch
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal chronicle of the zonal diversion incident that started 2026-03-11 02:12Z. This is a scratchpad: commands I ran, log excerpts, hypotheses to test, and short repro notes. Use/skip freely; __not a runbook__ (yet).

Background:
- Smart routing policy 'latency-pref' was active for customer cluster west-eu-prod.
- Autoscaler triggered burst to az1 and az3. At ~02:12 we started seeing route_eject events and an unusual spike in regional-diversion decisions: requests normally pinned to eu-west-1 -> were diverted to eu-west-2 and eu-central-1.

What I saw (top-line):
- Client latencies p95 jumped 350ms -> 1.2s in region.
- Router logs show repeated handshake timeouts to az1 edge (timeout ~2500ms).
- Route decisions triggered fallback to 'regional-closest' variant but with a race: some requests retried; others were left in-flight and timed out.

Commands / artifacts I ran / looked at: (rough order)
1) Grepped router events:
   $ zcat router-logs-2026-03-11.gz | egrep "route_eject|divert|handshake" | tail -n 120
   sample: 2026-03-11T02:13:01Z router-1 route_eject reason=handshake-timeout region=eu-west-1 trace=trx-8a3b

2) Queried route-policy decisions via admin API:
   $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \ \
     "https://admin.internal/v1/route_decisions?region=eu-west-1&from=2026-03-11T02:10Z" | jq '.results[] | {id,reason,alt_region,latency_ms}'

3) Spot-checked edge pod logs for az1: kubectl logs -n edge edge-az1-7f8 -c edge-proxy --since=20m
   saw repeated: "WARN handshake: peer=10.34.12.9 timeout=2500ms conn=0xc2e4"

4) Kernel network counters on one affected node (az1):
   $ ssh node-az1-05 -- sudo ss -s
   TCP: in-cnt=112345 out-cnt=110993 orphan=0 tw=14 alloc=1024 mem=0
   No obvious socket leak, but netdev rx buffer drops increased by ~2.3k in the 10m window (dmesg: "pcie0 rx-err drop").

5) Packet capture (short) on edge interface while reproducing low-rps test:
   $ sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/az1-02.pcap port 443 and host 10.34.12.9 -c 500
   Observed 3x TLS handshakes that stalled waiting for server hello (server retransmission).

Reproductions attempted locally:
- ran a small vegeta load (50 RPS) against a rolling set of instances in eu-west-1 with header x-region=eu-west-1 to force routing: saw about 6% of requests diverted after ~90s.
- toggled fallback policy in non-prod to 'strict-local' and replayed: diversion dropped to <1% -> suggests diversion logic is sensitive to handshake latency signals.

Log snippets (sanitized):
- router: 2026-03-11T02:12:59Z router-3 decision=divert reason=handshake-latency region=eu-west-1 alt=eu-west-2 policy=latency-pref trace=trx-8a3b
- edge: 2026-03-11T02:13:00Z edge-az1 WARN "TLS handshake stalled" conn=0x34a2 peer=10.34.12.9
- kubelet: 2026-03-11T02:13:05Z kubelet node-az1 kubelet: pod evicted due to image-pull backoff (unrelated?)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Transient NIC/PCIe issues on a subset of az1 hosts caused degraded TLS performance -> handshake latency -> routers ejected routes. Evidence: kernel rx drops, tcpdump stalls, dmesg pcie-err.
2) A control-plane change (recent PR to TLS session resume) introduced behavior under load that increases server hello latency for some cipher suites. Evidence mixed: PR linked below; only observed on hosts running older openssl.
3) Router health probe threshold too sensitive to transient handshake jitter and causes aggressive ejection. Evidence: fallback to regional happens within 2 failed handshakes.

Quick mitigation timeline (what we did):
- 02:20Z: increased router handshake timeout from 2000ms -> 4000ms for eu-west-1 (hotfix flag) to see if ejections stop. Immediate reduction in diversions from ~5% -> 1.2%.
- 02:33Z: cordoned / reimaged 2 suspect az1 hosts. Diversions fell to <0.2% and client p95 recovered.

Follow-ups / TODOs (next steps):
- [ ] Collect full pcap for longer window on reimaged host; attach to JIRA-OPS-1782.
- [ ] Confirm firmware/driver versions on az1 fleet nodes vs rest of cluster. Likely PCIe firmware mismatch. Priya to check with infra.
- [ ] Run a controlled experiment: deploy canary with new TLS resume PR to non-prod and stress handshake path (vegeta with 90% new sessions). Compare server hello timings.
- [ ] Revisit router ejection policy: add a short backoff hysteresis so two transient handshakes don't cause permanent ejection. Create a tiny A/B config in lab.
- [ ] Build metric: "handshake-server-hello-ms" at the router and emit to tracing for 95/99.

Notes to self:
- Reimaging fixed immediate symptom but not root cause; prioritize firmware/driver matrix review.
- Keep admin hotflag for handshake-timeout around during the validation window; rollback plan must be documented in JIRA.

Attachment refs: 
- pcap sample: /mnt/ops-artifacts/pcaps/az1-2026-03-11-02.pcap (short)
- kube events dump: s3://ops-dumps/eu-west-1/2026-03-11/kube-events.json.gz

Open questions: 
- Why were only a small subset of az1 hosts affected? hardware/placement pattern?
- Any correlation with recent kernel updates pushed 2026-03-09?

If I forget: first place to look is router traces (trace ids shown above), then edge node dmesg for pcie errors. Keep this doc updated as we get firmware matrix.

-- Evan
